title: Who Is Efren Reyes? The Magician of Pool Explained for New Fans
description: Efren "The Magician" Reyes is pool's most beloved legend. Learn his story, biggest wins, Hall of Fame honors and what beginners can learn from his game.
body:
Picture a kid standing on a Coca-Cola crate so he can reach the pool table. Fast forward a few decades and that same kid is beating the best players on the planet, often from positions that look impossible. That is the story of Efren Reyes, the Filipino star everyone in pool calls "The Magician." If you have seen his clips go viral lately and wondered why people treat him like royalty, this guide is for you.

From a Manila pool hall to the world stage

Efren Reyes was born on August 26, 1954, in Pampanga in the Philippines. At about five years old he moved to Manila to live with an uncle who owned a pool hall. According to his biography, he swept up, slept on the tables and used crates to reach the playing surface. He is said to have won his first match for money at age nine.

That pool hall education paid off. Reyes grew up playing a rough-and-ready style that forced him to solve problems on the table, rather than just run easy patterns. Decades later, you can still see it in how he plays.

Why "The Magician" and why "Bata"?

The nickname "The Magician" comes from his creative shot-making, especially his kick shots, where the cue ball goes off one or more rails before it hits the target. Where most players see a snooker, Reyes sees a way out.

His other nickname, "Bata", is a Filipino word meaning "kid." Friends reportedly gave it to him to tell him apart from an older player who was also named Efren.

The big wins every fan should know

  • 1994 U.S. Open 9-Ball Championship: he beat Nick Varner in the final and became the first player from outside the United States to win the event.
  • 1999 WPA World Nine-ball Championship: a win that was later recognized as an official world title.
  • 2004 WPA World Eight-ball Championship: he came back from 0-4 down to beat Marlon Manalo 11-8, which made him the first player to win world titles in more than one pool discipline.
  • World Cup of Pool: he won with Francisco "Django" Bustamante in 2006 and 2009.
  • Derby City Classic: a long list of titles at Kentucky's famous pool festival.

He also won a famous "Color of Money" nine-ball race to 120 against Earl Strickland in Hong Kong, coming back from 17 racks down to win 120-117. That match is still talked about by pool fans today.

Honors and legacy

Reyes was inducted into the Billiard Congress of America Hall of Fame in 2003, the first Asian player to earn that honor. He entered the One Pocket Hall of Fame in 2004, and in 2024 he was part of the first World Billiards Hall of Fame class in Yushan, China. In his home country he has been named Sportsman of the Year by the Philippine Sportswriters Association more than once and was added to the Philippine Sports Hall of Fame in 2010. Today, the annual Asia vs. Europe event, the Reyes Cup, carries his name.

What beginners can steal from The Magician

You will not copy Efren's touch overnight, but you can borrow his habits:

  • Think before you shoot. Look at every option, including defense. Our guide to safety play shows how to leave your opponent stuck.
  • Learn the rails. Kick shots and bank shots reward players who understand angles. Try our diamond system guide and the mirror method for kick shots.
  • Stay calm. Coming back from 0-4 or 17 racks down only works if you keep believing in the next shot.
  • Be creative, but sensible. Reyes takes risks only when he has judged the odds. Fancy shots are fun; smart shots win matches.

Why his clips keep going viral

Pool is a game of angles, and Reyes makes angles look friendly. His clips travel because anyone can understand the moment: the cue ball is trapped, the crowd leans in, and somehow the shot works anyway. You do not need to know the rules to enjoy that. It is also a nice reminder that pool is a game of imagination as much as strength.

Another reason fans love him is his calm manner. He is famous for playing with a relaxed, almost sleepy look while the pressure is at its highest. For newer players, that is a handy lesson: a quiet routine, steady breathing and trust in your stroke beat tense, rushed shooting almost every time.

Pool has produced many great champions over the years, but few are cheered by fans of every country the way Reyes is. If you are new to the sport, searching for his matches is one of the best ways to see how enjoyable the game can be to watch.

Where to watch great pool next

If Efren clips have you hungry for more, the next big stage is the Mosconi Cup, Team USA versus Team Europe, November 27-30 at the Caribe Royale in Orlando, Florida, with U.S. streaming on ESPN+ and the ESPN app per the Matchroom announcement. Read our Mosconi Cup 2026 hub for the latest, and browse the big tournaments page to find the next event on the calendar.

The bottom line

Efren Reyes is proof that creativity, patience and a love of the game can take someone from a Manila pool hall to the Hall of Fame. Next time a clip of him pulls off a wild shot, you will know the history behind the magic. Which Efren shot is your favorite? Tell us on our Facebook Page.
